notes: Landed at Utah south of the planned beach; 21,000 troops ashore for 197 casualties; not all D-Day objectives met. [Review 5: personnel changed from 21,000 (Wikipedia Normandy landings) to 20,000 with scope sector. CMH ch. 3 says the whole 4th Division except one field artillery battalion landed in the first fifteen hours, together with attached battalions and other units, and that over 20,000 troops in all reached Utah Beach by the end of 6 June; so the figure covers the whole force landed at Utah, not the division alone. The 197 casualties are the division's own (CMH).]

current_activity: attacking Azeville and Crisbecq fortified positions
notes: Two regiments pushed the enemy back about two miles to strongly fortified positions at Azeville and Crisbecq on D+1.
Attack north on the east coast; exhausted Montebourg-line defenders collapsed, little resistance 19-20 June.

current_activity: attacking Cherbourg defences from the east toward Tourlaville
notes: 4th Division attacked the Cherbourg defences from the east; 12th Infantry with tanks gathering momentum toward Tourlaville on 23 June (objective not reached that day).
4th Division took over security of Cherbourg after its fall; began moving south 30 June (relieved by 101st AB).

current_activity: a regiment tries to cross the Our four miles south-east of St. Vith; the leading battalion is across by noon next day
notes: Event date: 29 January 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 3 p. 66: on the first day, 29 January, one regiment of the 4th Division tried to cross the Our four miles south-east of St. Vith; it was noon the next day before the whole leading battalion was across). Event definition: the division opens the VIII Corps attack on the West Wall; the row is the crossing sector of the right regiment. Relationship: VIII Corps unspecified_subordination (from 27 Jan 45 to 9 Mar 45, CMH table); Third Army assigned (from 20 Dec 44 to 9 Mar 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 1 Aug 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier assigned relation to First Army (CR0219) is closed at 19 December 1944 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. The earlier unspecified_subordination relation to V Corps (CR0222) is closed at 7 November 1944 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. Location: Saint-Vith, the town four miles north-west of the crossing the source names; no crossing site is named. Coordinates: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (St Vith, Liege, Belgium).
